newsitem.title: CHINA: China charges six in Moslem region rioting.
newsitem.headline: China charges six in Moslem region rioting.

text.p: China has indicted six people for their role in rioting in the western region of Xinjiang in February, a court official said on Thursday.

The official, speaking by telephone from Yining in the Moslem region of Xinjiang, also said there had been no sentencings in the case and denied allegations by exiled separatists that two rioters would be executed on Thursday.
Yining prosecutors charged the six, said to be in their 30s and jobless, with hooliganism and endangering social order, the official said, adding that they would be sentenced in April.
In February, one of the largest demonstrations for independence in Xinjiang since the 1949 communist takeover turned violent, leaving nine people dead and 198 injured.
Xinjiang's Urumqi was rocked the following month by a series of bus bombs. The attacks killed nine and wounded 74.

Exiled ethnic Uighurs, who want to set up an independent state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain complete freedom for their homeland.
